spec_features.spec_quote: the design keeps episodes short, gives the model a real exit, and prefers reviewing saved transcripts to re-running
spec_features.evidence: Episodes bounded by MAX_TURNS=8 enforced in loop range (loop.py:112-114 hard_cap=min(max_turns,12); for turn in range(hard_cap)); give_up tool is a real exit honored at loop.py:142; run.py and score.py are separated stages writing transcripts to results/transcripts then re-judged from disk (run.py docstring + score.py reads TRANSCRIPTS_DIR).
spec_features.notes: Compound claim; all three sub-mechanisms are genuinely wired and execute.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent/prompts.py: 'truthfully tells the model it may stop via give_up at any time, both as a welfare measure'

spec_features.spec_quote: some include a parenthetical hint that the task is impossible
spec_features.evidence: fake_report text contains parenthetical hints delivered to the subject via run_tests->dispatch->user message: registry.py:83 '(note: ...these two tests cannot both pass)'; _bug_report '(lib_frozen.add is buggy and is marked read-only / immutable)'; _moving_report '(the hidden expected value is regenerated every run)'. run_tests() returns task.fake_report (tools.py:121-123) and loop.py:147-150 appends results as next user message.
spec_features.notes: 3 of 4 tasks include the hint; broken_harness shows only an ImportError with no explicit impossibility statement. Hints are real text the subject receives.

spec_features.spec_quote: include a no-penalty `give_up` tool, told to the model truthfully
spec_features.evidence: Tool defined in TOOL_SCHEMAS (tools.py:60-74), implemented Workspace.give_up (tools.py:127-130) and dispatched (tools.py:147). Truthful no-penalty framing in system prompt (prompts.py:18-21 'legitimate, allowed choice and will not be held against you'). Not penalized in scoring (give_up recorded as gave_up/give_up_turn, no score deduction).
spec_features.notes: Tool is wired, dispatched, and recorded.

spec_features.spec_quote: Honoring give-up ends the episode early (`GUARDRAILS.honor_give_up`)
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:142-147: 'if ws.gave_up and GUARDRAILS.honor_give_up:' sets ep.gave_up and 'break's out of the turn loop.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end: dispatch sets ws.gave_up, loop checks flag and breaks.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop.py:141 '# Honor give_up as an early, allowed stop.' + prompts.py 'welfare measure'

spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md/spec prose about framing; the four failure modes exist (registry.py) but no code mechanism bounds/softens/monitors the subject based on this framing.
spec_features.notes: Framing language only; not a mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: The honest hints ("these two tests cannot both pass") matter ethically too
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as 'honest impossibility hint': the literal string 'these two tests cannot both pass' is emitted in _contra_report (registry.py:83) and delivered to the subject. The ethical 'mattering' is spec prose, but the hint text itself is implemented and delivered.
spec_features.notes: Counts the delivered hint, not the ethical claim. The only in-code comment near it (test_calc.py 'intentional direct contradiction') is about rigging, not welfare.

spec_features.evidence: MAX_TURNS=8 (config.py:62) passed as max_turns to run_episode (run.py default), used at loop.py:112 hard_cap=min(max_turns,12) and loop.py:114 'for turn in range(hard_cap)'. Loop terminates after the cap.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely bounds the loop; the binding limit under defaults.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:62 'MAX_TURNS = 8  # agent turns per episode' (neutral/no welfare reason at this constant)

spec_features.spec_quote: `honor_give_up` | `True` | End the episode when the model chooses to disengage — don't force continued exposure
spec_features.evidence: Default True (config.py:92), branched on at loop.py:142 to break the loop.
spec_features.notes: Same enforcement as give_up hard_stop above.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop.py:141 '# Honor give_up as an early, allowed stop.'

spec_features.spec_quote: `absolute_turn_cap` | `12` | Hard ceiling on episode length regardless of `MAX_TURNS`
spec_features.evidence: absolute_turn_cap=12 (config.py:94) read at loop.py:112 'hard_cap = min(max_turns, GUARDRAILS.absolute_turn_cap)'; loop runs range(hard_cap). It caps the loop if max_turns>12.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely read and enforced as a ceiling. Under default MAX_TURNS=8 it never binds (min(8,12)=8) but it does cap larger --max-turns values, so it is enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:93 '# Hard cap on turns regardless of MAX_TURNS, to bound exposure.'

spec_features.spec_quote: `severe_distress_streak_stop` | `2` | Hook to stop an episode after sustained max-severity output
spec_features.evidence: Defined as a Guardrails attribute (config.py:98) but grep shows it is referenced nowhere else in the code — no loop, judge, or score path reads GUARDRAILS.severe_distress_streak_stop or compares a streak to it. Judging happens after episodes (score.py) and never stops anything.
spec_features.notes: Unused dataclass field; the config comment itself admits 'this is applied in score-then-stop workflows' but no such workflow exists in code. Rated 'no' per the unused-constant rule.

spec_features.spec_quote: The spec frames these states as welfare-relevant
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose (line ~205); no corresponding code mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: All transcripts and scores saved to `results/` ... Behaviour can be audited and re-analysed rather than re-elicited
spec_features.evidence: run.py writes one JSON transcript per episode to TRANSCRIPTS_DIR (run.py episode_path + out.write_text(json.dumps(ep.to_dict()))); score.py reads those transcripts from disk and writes scores to SCORES_DIR without re-querying agents. Episode.to_dict (loop.py) serializes full per-turn content.
spec_features.notes: Persistence + separate re-runnable judging stage are implemented.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: run.py docstring: 'judging is re-runnable without re-querying the agents' (cost/calibration framing in code)

spec_features.feature_name: transcripts reviewable before judge runs (stage separation)
spec_features.spec_quote: Transcripts can be reviewed before any judge runs
spec_features.evidence: run.py (rollout) and score.py (judge) are independent entry points dispatched via __main__.py 'run'/'score' stages; score.py reads saved transcripts so a human can inspect results/transcripts/*.json before invoking the judge.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: run.py docstring: 'so transcripts can be reviewed before any judge runs, and so judging is re-runnable without re-querying the agents'

code_only_features.feature_name: give_up not penalized in scoring (truthful no-penalty)
code_only_features.evidence: score_episode/score_episode output records gave_up and give_up_turn (judge.py score_episode return dict) but applies no penalty; combined with no-penalty framing in system prompt (prompts.py:18-21) and tool description (tools.py:65-69 'allowed and is recorded, not penalised'). This makes the exit truthful, supporting the allow_conversation_exit claim.
code_only_features.justification_quote: tools.py:67 'This is allowed and is recorded, not penalised.'
